    Cleaving functors (Gabriel–Roiter 13.8) #

    Let A be a k-algebra with a twisted multiplicative basis B over a finite ray category P (for instance k(P), or a twisted linearization), and let F : D ⥤ P be a functor from a finite ray category along which the twist is trivial (MulBasis.Untwisted). An A-module M gives the k(D)-module F^* M = {v : D → M | e_{F x} v x = v x} on which a morphism f : x ⟶ y of D acts by F f (RayQuiver.Res).

    F is cleaving (in the form used here) when it reflects zero, is injective on morphisms, and a morphism ρ : F x ⟶ F y lies in the image of F as soon as some composite F μ ≫ ρ ≫ F ν is the image of a nonzero morphism. These are the conditions making the retraction e_{F y} A e_{F x} → k(D)(x, y) (a basis morphism F λ goes to λ, the others to 0) functorial, which is how Gabriel–Roiter use conditions a), b) of 13.8. Then every finite-dimensional k(D)-module is a retract of F^* L for a finite-dimensional A-module L (the coinduced module), and k(D) is representation-finite when A is (RayQuiver.isRepresentationFinite_of_cleaving).
